content:
alex: Thinking out loud — can we run a controlled chaos sim against our spot GPU pools next Thurs to validate fallback capacity + cross-region reshuffle? want to test: sudden 30-50% spot evictions in us-west1 and eu-west1, and verify routing + hot-standby warm pool behavior.

maria: sgtm. scope: two clusters (prod-gpu-us, prod-gpu-eu) with different nodepool mixes. keep rps low; this is infra test not perf.

ajay: recommend window 0200–0400 UTC, low traffic. we should disable automatic scaling to avoid noisy autoscaler interference, then replay our autoscaler logic via a canary controller.

jin: cost note — running warm standby 100 gpus for 2h ~= $Xk. can we reduce by using 1/3 capacity + synthetic traffic that triggers model shards?

maria: agree. suggested plan:
- spin up warm-standby nodepool in secondary region with taint `standby=true:NoSchedule`
- pre-pull checkpoint / model cache to reduce cold-starts
- run eviction script in primary region nodes that simulates spot termination (SIGTERM + drain)
- validate fallback routing in the control plane

ajay: autoscaler config snippet I used last time (paste):
```yaml
apiVersion: autoscaling/v1
kind: VerticalPodAutoscaler
metadata:
  name: gpu-serving-vpa
spec:
  updatePolicy:
    updateMode: "Off" # keep manual for test
```
not exhaustive but we should pin updateMode off.

alex: what about preemption handling? our termination-handler currently waits for GCE preemptible 30s notice and then tries to drain; if we simulate abrupt OS-level stop we need to exercise our fallback to dedicated pool.

maria: add a synthetic short-notice path: terminate via cloud API with no graceful window. that will exercise immediate routing fallbacks and warm pool burst. log expectations: 1) model-serving pods restarted in standby 2) traffic rerouted via smart router 3) no 5xx spike > 0.5%

jin: add alerting checklist:
- trace rate 95p latency per-route
- new cold-start count (model loads)
- failed allocations from scheduler
- cost burn vs baseline

ops-bot: scheduled: chaos-slot-2026-02-12T02:00Z by alex (owner). automated rollback hook enabled.

ajay: I'll create the job artifacts. quick commands we will run in the sim:
```
# cordon + drain simulated nodes
kubectl cordon gpu-preempt-1
kubectl drain gpu-preempt-1 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
# simulate instant stop (cloud API)
gcloud compute instances stop gpu-preempt-1 --zone=us-west1-b --no-wait
```

maria: also include a canary config for router so we can target 10% traffic to fallback path first:
```
route:
  fallback_percent: 10
  fallback_models: [gptq-13b-quant, gpt-13b-fp16]
```

jin: i'll pre-create dashboards and a cost tag so finance can match charges. will block a small slack thread for finance if we need overrides.

alex: one more — make sure quota bump requests for secondary region are in (GPUs + IPs). last time we hit ephemeral IP quota when scaling warm pool.

ajay: noted. hitting up cloud-quotas@ for temporary bump.

k8s-scaler-bot: [info] prod-gpu-us autoscaler: current nodes 420 -> target 420 (manual override enabled)

maria: runbook snippet for on-call if things blow up:
- pause test (ops-bot)
- revert router to primary-only
- scale down standby pools
- open priority incident channel and call product impacts

alex: timeline: prep by Wed EOD (artifacts + quota + dashboards), run Thu 02:00–04:00 UTC, postmortem Fri. volunteers?

maria: i'll own model pre-pulls and taints.

ajay: infra job + termination scripts — i'll run and monitor.

jin: dashboards + finance tags.

alex: perfect. keeping it small and reversible. will post final checklist tomorrow. :thumbsup:
